The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# hostctl

[![Your dev tool to manage /etc/hosts like a pro!](docs/hostctl.png)](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/)

This tool gives you more control over the use of your hosts file. 
You can have multiple profiles and switch them on/off as you need.

## Why?

It is a tedious task to handle the `hosts` file by editing manually.
With this tool you can automate some aspects to do it cleaner and quick. 

## Features

  * Manage groups of host names by profile.
  * Enable/disable complete profiles.
  * Add/remove groups of host names.
  * Add profiles directly from a text file that you can add to your git repo or any VCS.
  * Sync a profile with Docker or Docker Compose containers.

## Documentation

You can read about how to use this tool here:

* [Getting started guide](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/getting-started/) 
* [Usage Guides](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/guides/)
* [CLI commands, options and flags](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/cli-usage/)

Or you can start directly on the [Docs homepage](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/).

## Sample Usage

![sample usage](docs/hostctl.gif)

## Installation

Go to [release page](https://github.com/guumaster/hostctl/releases) and download the binary you prefer.

Or read about other installation methods on different systems [here](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/installation/)

## Linux/Mac/Windows and permissions

The tool recognize your system and use the right hosts file, it will use `/etc/hosts` on Linux/Mac and `C:/Windows/System32/Drivers/etc/hosts` on Windows.

**SUDO/ADMIN**: You will need permissions for any action that modify hosts file, add `sudo` to the commands below when needed. If you are on windows, make sure you run it as administrator.

**WARNING**: it should work on any system. It's tested on Ubuntu and Windows 10. If you can confirm it works on other system, please let me know [here](https://github.com/guumaster/hostctl/issues/new).

## LICENSE

[MIT license](LICENSE)

# hostctl

[![Your dev tool to manage /etc/hosts like a pro!](docs/hostctl.png)](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/)

This tool gives you more control over the use of your hosts file. 
You can have multiple profiles and switch them on/off as you need.

## Why?

It is a tedious task to handle the `hosts` file by editing manually.
With this tool you can automate some aspects to do it cleaner and quick. 

## Features

  * Manage groups of host names by profile.
  * Enable/disable complete profiles.
  * Add/remove groups of host names.
  * Add profiles directly from a text file that you can add to your git repo or any VCS.
  * Sync a profile with Docker or Docker Compose containers.

## Documentation

You can read about how to use this tool here:

* [Getting started guide](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/getting-started/) 
* [Usage Guides](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/guides/)
* [CLI commands, options and flags](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/cli-usage/)

Or you can start directly on the [Docs homepage](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/).

## Sample Usage

![sample usage](docs/hostctl.gif)

## Installation

Go to [release page](https://github.com/guumaster/hostctl/releases) and download the binary you prefer.

Or read about other installation methods on different systems [here](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/installation/)

## Linux/Mac/Windows and permissions

The tool recognize your system and use the right hosts file, it will use `/etc/hosts` on Linux/Mac and `C:/Windows/System32/Drivers/etc/hosts` on Windows.

**SUDO/ADMIN**: You will need permissions for any action that modify hosts file, add `sudo` to the commands below when needed. If you are on windows, make sure you run it as administrator.

**WARNING**: it should work on any system. It's tested on Ubuntu and Windows 10. If you can confirm it works on other system, please let me know [here](https://github.com/guumaster/hostctl/issues/new).

# bash completion for hostctl                              -*- shell-script -*-

__hostctl_debug()
{
    if [[ -n ${BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE:-} ]]; then
        echo "$*" >> "${BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE}"
    fi
}

# Homebrew on Macs have version 1.3 of bash-completion which doesn't include
# _init_completion. This is a very minimal version of that function.
__hostctl_init_completion()
{
    COMPREPLY=()
    _get_comp_words_by_ref "$@" cur prev words cword
}

__hostctl_index_of_word()
{
    local w word=$1
    shift
    index=0
    for w in "$@"; do
        [[ $w = "$word" ]] && return
        index=$((index+1))
    done
    index=-1
}

__hostctl_contains_word()
{
    local w word=$1; shift
    for w in "$@"; do
        [[ $w = "$word" ]] && return
    done
    return 1
}

__hostctl_handle_go_custom_completion()
{
    __hostctl_debug "${FUNCNAME[0]}: cur is ${cur}, words[*] is ${words[*]}, #words[@] is ${#words[@]}"

    local shellCompDirectiveError=1
    local shellCompDirectiveNoSpace=2
    local shellCompDirectiveNoFileComp=4
    local shellCompDirectiveFilterFileExt=8
    local shellCompDirectiveFilterDirs=16

    local out requestComp lastParam lastChar comp directive args

    # Prepare the command to request completions for the program.
    # Calling ${words[0]} instead of directly hostctl allows to handle aliases
    args=("${words[@]:1}")
    # Disable ActiveHelp which is not supported for bash completion v1
    requestComp="HOSTCTL_ACTIVE_HELP=0 ${words[0]} __completeNoDesc ${args[*]}"

    lastParam=${words[$((${#words[@]}-1))]}
    lastChar=${lastParam:$((${#lastParam}-1)):1}
    __hostctl_debug "${FUNCNAME[0]}: lastParam ${lastParam}, lastChar ${lastChar}"

    if [ -z "${cur}" ] && [ "${lastChar}" != "=" ]; then
        # If the last parameter is complete (there is a space following it)
        # We add an extra empty parameter so we can indicate this to the go method.
        __hostctl_debug "${FUNCNAME[0]}: Adding extra empty parameter"
        requestComp="${requestComp} \"\""
    fi

    __hostctl_debug "${FUNCNAME[0]}: calling ${requestComp}"
    # Use eval to handle any environment variables and such
    out=$(eval "${requestComp}" 2>/dev/null)

    # Extract the directive integer at the very end of the output following a colon (:)
    directive=${out##*:}
    # Remove the directive
    out=${out%:*}
    if [ "${directive}" = "${out}" ]; then
        # There is not directive specified
        directive=0
    fi
    __hostctl_debug "${FUNCNAME[0]}: the completion directive is: ${directive}"
    __hostctl_debug "${FUNCNAME[0]}: the completions are: ${out}"

    if [ $((directive & shellCompDirectiveError)) -ne 0 ]; then
        # Error code.  No completion.
        __hostctl_debug "${FUNCNAME[0]}: received error from custom completion go code"
        return
    else
        if [ $((directive & shellCompDirectiveNoSpace)) -ne 0 ]; then

import subprocess

        print(w,"TIMEOUT",repr(e.stdout))
PY

import subprocess, os, shutil
ORIG="/workspace/executable"; MINE="/tmp/myhostctl"
BASE="127.0.0.1 localhost\n\n##################################################################\n# Content under this line is handled by hostctl. DO NOT EDIT.\n##################################################################\n\n# profile.on p1\n1.1.1.1 a.com\n1.1.1.1 b.com\n# end\n\n# profile.off p2\n# 2.2.2.2 c.com\n# end\n"
def setup(root, content=BASE):
    shutil.rmtree(root,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(root)
    open(root+"/hosts","w").write(content)
    open(root+"/in.txt","w").write("10.0.0.1 one.com two.com\n# comment\n10.0.0.2 three.com\ninvalid bad.com\n10.0.0.1 four.com\n")
    open(root+"/restore.txt","w").write("9.9.9.9 restored.com extra.com\n")
    os.makedirs(root+"/bk",exist_ok=True)
def run(exe,root,args,stdin_data=None):
    a=[x.replace("{h}",root+"/hosts").replace("{in}",root+"/in.txt").replace("{r}",root+"/restore.txt").replace("{bk}",root+"/bk") for x in args]
    if stdin_data is None:
        r=subprocess.run([exe]+a,stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,capture_output=True,text=True,cwd=root)
    else:
        r=subprocess.run([exe]+a,input=stdin_data,capture_output=True,text=True,cwd=root)
    files={}
    for fn in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        p=os.path.join(root,fn)
        if os.path.isfile(p): files[fn]=open(p).read()
    # include bk dir
    for dirpath,_,filenames in os.walk(root):
        for fn in filenames:
            p=os.path.join(dirpath,fn); rel=os.path.relpath(p,root); files[rel]=open(p).read()
    return r.returncode,r.stdout,r.stderr,files
cases=[
 ["--host-file","{h}","add","newp","--from","{in}"],
 ["--host-file","{h}","add","p1","--from","{in}"],
 ["--host-file","{h}","replace","p1","--from","{in}"],
 ["--host-file","{h}","replace","newp","--from","{in}"],
 ["--host-file","{h}","add","newp"],
 ["--host-file","{h}","add","newp","--from","/nonexist"],
 ["--host-file","{h}","backup","--path","{bk}"],
 ["--host-file","{h}","backup"],
 ["--host-file","{h}","backup","--path","/nonexistdir"],
 ["--host-file","{h}","restore","--from","{r}"],
 ["--host-file","{h}","restore"],
 ["--host-file","{h}","restore","--from","/nonexist"],
 ["--host-file","{h}","restore","--from","/tmp"],
]
fails=0
for args in cases:
    setup("/tmp/dto"); o=run(ORIG,"/tmp/dto",args)
    setup("/tmp/dtm"); m=run(MINE,"/tmp/dtm",args)
    # backup default cwd differs root dto/dtm path in stdout/files keys? backup command default path is cwd root, stdout includes root path so will differ. Replace roots for comparison
    def norm(x): return (x[0],x[1].replace("/tmp/dto","ROOT").replace("/tmp/dtm","ROOT"),x[2],{k.replace("/tmp/dto","ROOT"):v for k,v in x[3].items()})
    if norm(o)!=norm(m):
        fails+=1; print("DIFF",args); print(" orig",norm(o)); print(" mine",norm(m))
# stdin cases
for args, data in [(["--host-file","{h}","add","stdinprof"],"9.9.9.9 stdin.com\n"), (["--host-file","{h}","add","stdinprof","--from","{in}"],"9.9.9.9 stdin.com\n"), (["--host-file","{h}","replace","p1"],"8.8.8.8 repl.com\n"), (["--host-file","{h}","add","emptyp"],"" )]:
    setup("/tmp/dto"); o=run(ORIG,"/tmp/dto",args,data)
    setup("/tmp/dtm"); m=run(MINE,"/tmp/dtm",args,data)
    if o!=m:
        fails+=1; print("DIFF stdin",args); print(" orig",o); print(" mine",m)
print("fails",fails)

import subprocess, pty, os, signal, time
def run_pty(exe,args,term="xterm-256color",sig=None):
    env=dict(os.environ); env["TERM"]=term
    master, slave=pty.openpty()
    p=subprocess.Popen([exe]+args, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, stdin=slave, env=env)
    os.close(slave)
    if sig:
        time.sleep(0.4); p.send_signal(sig)
    data=b""
    while True:
        try: chunk=os.read(master,4096)
        except OSError: break
        if not chunk: break
        data+=chunk
    try: p.wait(timeout=3)
    except: p.kill()
    os.close(master)
    return p.returncode, data
BASE="127.0.0.1 localhost\n\n##################################################################\n# Content under this line is handled by hostctl. DO NOT EDIT.\n##################################################################\n\n# profile.off p1\n# 1.1.1.1 a.com\n# end\n"
for exe in ["/workspace/executable","/tmp/myhostctl"]:
    open("/tmp/dt/hosts","w").write(BASE)
    print(exe, run_pty(exe,["--host-file","/tmp/dt/hosts","list"]))
    open("/tmp/dt/hosts","w").write(BASE)
    print(exe, run_pty(exe,["--host-file","/tmp/dt/hosts","enable","nope"]))
    open("/tmp/dt/hosts","w").write(BASE)
    print(exe, run_pty(exe,["--host-file","/tmp/dt/hosts","--no-color","list"]))
    print(exe, run_pty(exe,["--no-color","badcmd"]))
    open("/tmp/dt/hosts","w").write(BASE)
    print(exe, "sigint wait", run_pty(exe,["--host-file","/tmp/dt/hosts","enable","--wait","0s","p1"],sig=signal.SIGINT))
    print(exe, "file", open("/tmp/dt/hosts").read())

import subprocess, pty, os, signal, time
def run_pty(exe,args,term="xterm-256color",sig=None):
    env=dict(os.environ); env["TERM"]=term
    master, slave=pty.openpty()
    p=subprocess.Popen([exe]+args, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, stdin=slave, env=env)
    os.close(slave)
    if sig:
        time.sleep(0.4); p.send_signal(sig)
    data=b""
    while True:
        try: chunk=os.read(master,4096)
        except OSError: break
        if not chunk: break
        data+=chunk
    try: p.wait(timeout=3)
    except: p.kill()
    os.close(master)
    return p.returncode, data

import socket, os, threading, json, sys
mode=sys.argv[1]
sockpath="/tmp/fake-docker.sock"
try: os.unlink(sockpath)
except: pass
srv=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM); srv.bind(sockpath); srv.listen(5)
def handle(c):
    data=b""
    while b"\r\n\r\n" not in data:
        ch=c.recv(4096)
        if not ch: break
        data+=ch
    path=data.decode(errors='ignore').split(" ")[1]
    if mode=="error500":
        body=b'{"message":"daemon exploded"}'; code=b"500 Internal Server Error"
    elif mode=="badjson":
        body=b'not json'; code=b"200 OK"
    elif mode=="objcontainers":
        body=b'{}'; code=b"200 OK"
    elif mode=="objnetworks":
        if "networks" in path: body=b'{}'
        else: body=b'[]'
        code=b"200 OK"
    elif mode=="emptyname":
        body=json.dumps([{"Id":"1","Names":[],"NetworkSettings":{"Networks":{"bridge":{"NetworkID":"n1","IPAddress":"10.0.0.1"}}}}]).encode(); code=b"200 OK"
    else:
        body=b'[]'; code=b"200 OK"
    c.sendall(b"HTTP/1.1 "+code+b"\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: "+str(len(body)).encode()+b"\r\n\r\n"+body); c.close()
while True:
    c,_=srv.accept(); threading.Thread(target=handle,args=(c,),daemon=True).start()

func doAddDomains(profileName string, domains []string, ipStr string, wait time.Duration) error {
	hf, err := loadHostsFile()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	p := hf.findProfile(profileName)
	if p == nil {
		p = &Profile{Name: profileName, Status: "on"}
		hf.Profiles = append(hf.Profiles, p)
	}
	ip := net.ParseIP(ipStr)
	for _, d := range domains {
		p.AddRoute(ip, d)
	}
	if err := hf.flush(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	reloaded, err := loadHostsFile()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	printSuccessMessage(fmt.Sprintf("Domains '%s' added.", strings.Join(domains, ", ")))
	printRendered(renderGroups(profilesGroupsFiltered(reloaded, []string{profileName}), false), true, true)
	return nil
}

func doRemoveDomains(profileName string, domains []string) error {
	hf, err := loadHostsFile()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	p := hf.findProfile(profileName)
	if p == nil {
		return errUnknownProfile
	}
	for _, d := range domains {
		p.RemoveDomain(d)
	}
	removed := p.RouteCount() == 0
	if removed {
		hf.removeProfile(profileName)
	}
	if err := hf.flush(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	reloaded, err := loadHostsFile()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if removed {
		printSuccessMessage(fmt.Sprintf("Profile '%s' removed.", profileName))
		printRendered(renderGroups([]rowGroup{{Rows: nil}}, false), false, true)
		return nil
	}
	printSuccessMessage(fmt.Sprintf("Domains '%s' removed.", strings.Join(domains, ", ")))
	rp := reloaded.findProfile(profileName)
	printRendered(renderGroups(profileRenderGroups(reloaded, rp), false), false, true)
	return nil
}

func readInputProfile(name string, from string) (*Profile, error) {
	prof := &Profile{Name: name, Status: "on"}
	var lines []string
	stat, _ := os.Stdin.Stat()
	if stat != nil && (stat.Mode()&os.ModeCharDevice) == 0 {
		scanner := makeScanner(os.Stdin)
		lines = readLinesFromReader(scanner)
	} else {
		f, err := os.Open(from)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		defer f.Close()
		lines = readLinesFromReader(makeScanner(f))
	}
	parseRoutesInto(lines, prof)
	return prof, nil
}

func doAddFromInput(name string, from string, replace bool) error {
	inputProf, err := readInputProfile(name, from)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	hf, err := loadHostsFile()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if replace {
		hf.removeProfile(name)
		hf.Profiles = append(hf.Profiles, inputProf)
	} else {
		if existing := hf.findProfile(name); existing != nil {
			existing.MergeRoutes(inputProf)
		} else {
			hf.Profiles = append(hf.Profiles, inputProf)
		}
	}
	if err := hf.flush(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	reloaded, err := loadHostsFile()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if replace {
		printRendered(renderGroups(profilesGroupsFiltered(reloaded, []string{name}), false), false, true)
	} else {
		printRendered(renderGroups(profilesGroupsFiltered(reloaded, []string{name}), false), true, true)
	}
	return nil
}

func doReplaceProfileWithRoutes(name string, routes []docker.Route) error {
	hf, err := loadHostsFile()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	prof := &Profile{Name: name, Status: "on"}
	for _, r := range routes {
		prof.AddRoute(net.ParseIP(r.IP), r.Domain)
	}
	hf.removeProfile(name)
	hf.Profiles = append(hf.Profiles, prof)
	if err := hf.flush(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	reloaded, err := loadHostsFile()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	printRendered(renderGroups(profilesGroupsFiltered(reloaded, []string{name}), false), true, true)
	return nil
}

func copyFile(src string, dst string) error {
	in, err := os.Open(src)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer in.Close()
	out, err := os.Create(dst)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer out.Close()
	_, err = io.Copy(out, in)
	return err
}

// ---------------- wait handling ----------------

func handleWait(waitDur time.Duration, revertDesc string, waitArgs []string, revert func() error) error {
	if waitDur < 0 {
		return nil
	}
	if !opts.quiet {
		var msg string
		if waitDur == 0 {
			msg = fmt.Sprintf("Waiting until ctrl+c to %s from profile '%s'", revertDesc, strings.Join(waitArgs, ", "))
		} else {
			msg = fmt.Sprintf("Waiting for %s or ctrl+c to %s from profile '%s'", waitDur.String(), revertDesc, strings.Join(waitArgs, ", "))
		}
		printInfoMessage(msg)
	}
	waitForSignalOrTimeout(waitDur)
	if opts.quiet {
		fmt.Println()
	} else {
		fmt.Print("\n\n")
	}
	return revert()
